en: to be wide; to be spacious
ko_meaning_en: For a place such as a room or road to be big

example.en: This room is spacious and quiet.

form.q_en: Pick the right '-고' (and) form of 넓다.
form.why: -고 attaches straight to the stem 넓-, so it is 넓고. The ㄼ in the stem never drops in writing.

en: to be narrow; to be cramped
ko_meaning_en: For the space of a road or room to be small

example.ko: 이 길은 좁아서 차가 못 가요.
example.roman: I gireun jobaseo chaga mot gayo.
example.en: This road is narrow so cars can't get through.

form.q_en: Pick the form that gives the reason ('so').
form.why: 좁다 is regular (the ㅂ stays) and its stem has ㅗ, so it takes -아서: 좁아서.

ko_meaning_en: For the length to not be long

example.en: My younger sister likes short skirts.

tokens.note: -은 makes an adjective describe a noun

form.q_en: Pick the noun-modifier form of 짧다 ('short skirts').
form.why: Adjectives take -(으)ㄴ before a noun. 짧- ends in a consonant, so it is 짧은. -는 is for verbs.

ko_meaning_en: There is a lot of light so you can see well

example.en: The window is big so the room is bright.

tokens.note: 이 marks the subject after a consonant

form.q_en: Pick the right polite form of 밝다.
form.why: 밝다 has ㅏ in the stem, so it takes -아요: 밝아요 (said [발가요]).

ko_meaning_en: There is no light so you can't see well

example.en: The park is dark at night so it's scary.

form.q_en: Pick the right '-아서/어서' form of 어둡다.
form.why: 어둡다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우 before a vowel, so 어두 + 워서 → 어두워서.

ko_meaning_en: For two things to not be different from each other

example.en: My younger brother and I have the same birthday.

form.q_en: Pick the right polite form of 같다.
form.why: 같다 has ㅏ in the stem, so it takes -아요: 같아요 (said [가타요]).

ko_meaning_en: For things to not be the same as each other

example.en: These two bags are different colors.

tokens.note: 둘 becomes 두 before a noun

form.q_en: Pick the right polite form of 다르다.
form.why: 다르다 is 르-irregular: 르 drops, ㄹ is added and the stem vowel ㅏ brings -아요: 달라요.

ko_meaning: 답이 틀리지 않다; 옷이나 신발의 크기가 몸에 좋다
ko_meaning_en: An answer is not wrong; clothes or shoes are the right size

example.en: The teacher is right.

form.q_en: My answer is not right. Pick the form before 않아요.
form.why: -지 않다 makes a negative: the stem 맞- + 지 않아요 = 'is not right'.

ko_meaning_en: An answer or idea is not right

example.en: I got two questions wrong on the test.

form.q_en: Pick the right past form of 틀리다.
form.why: 틀리 + 었어요 contracts to 틀렸어요 (ㅣ + ㅓ → ㅕ).

ko_meaning_en: Something must be there

example.en: I need a big bag for the trip.

tokens.note: -ㄴ makes an adjective describe a noun
the needed thing is the subject

form.q_en: With 필요하다, which particle does the needed thing take?
form.why: 필요하다 is an adjective, so the needed thing is the subject. 가방 ends in a consonant, so 이 (not 가). 을 would be wrong.

ko_meaning_en: To be warm-hearted and nice to other people

example.en: The man at this store is really kind.

form.q_en: The man is kind, so I'll go again. Pick the reason form with -(으)니까.
form.why: -(으)니까 gives a reason. 친절하- ends in a vowel, so just add -니까: 친절하니까.

ko_meaning: 마음이 좋고 다른 사람을 잘 생각하다
ko_meaning_en: To have a good heart and care about others

example.en: My younger brother is good-natured and cute.

form.q_en: My brother is good-natured BUT noisy. Pick the 'but' form.
form.why: -지만 means 'but' and attaches straight to the stem: 착하 + 지만 → 착하지만.

ko_meaning_en: Many people know it well

example.en: This restaurant is famous for its bulgogi.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: It's famous, so there are many people. Pick the reason form.
form.why: 하다 + 아서 becomes 해서: 유명해서 = 'because it is famous'.

ko_meaning_en: To not be old in age

example.en: Young people like this cafe.

form.q_en: Pick the noun-modifier form of 젊다.
form.why: 젊다 is an adjective ending in a consonant, so before a noun it takes -은: 젊은.

ko_meaning_en: To become older in age

example.en: Grandpa's dog has gotten very old.

tokens.note: 늙다 is a verb, so 'is old' uses the past

form.q_en: 늙다 is a verb, so 'has grown old' uses the past tense. Pick it.
form.why: 늙다 has ㅡ in the stem, so it takes -었어요: 늙었어요 (said [늘거써요]).

ko_meaning_en: To bring something new into being

example.en: I made rice cakes with Mom on the weekend.

form.q_en: Pick the right future form of 만들다.
form.why: 만들- already ends in ㄹ, so -(으)ㄹ 거예요 adds nothing more: 만들 거예요.

ko_meaning: 필요한 것이 어디에 있는지 알려고 하다
ko_meaning_en: To try to learn where something you need is

example.en: I found a Korean book at the library.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the form that means 'go (in order) to look for'.
form.why: -(으)러 shows purpose before 가다/오다. 찾- ends in a consonant, so it takes -으러: 찾으러.

ko_meaning_en: Something you had goes missing

example.en: I lost my umbrella on the subway.

form.q_en: I lost my umbrella, so I bought a new one. Pick the reason form.
form.why: 버리 + 어서 contracts to 버려서. Don't add the past tense before -아서/어서.

ko_meaning: 물건이나 편지를 다른 곳으로 가게 하다
ko_meaning_en: To make a thing or letter go somewhere else

example.en: I sent a letter at the post office.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the right past form of 보내다.
form.why: 보내 + 었어요 contracts to 보냈어요.

ko_meaning_en: To take what someone gives you

example.en: I got a lot of flowers on my birthday.

form.q_en: Can I get a receipt? Pick the form before 수 있어요.
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 = can. 받- ends in a consonant, so it is 받을 수 있어요.

ko_meaning: 모르는 것을 알 수 있게 알려 주다
ko_meaning_en: To show someone what they don't know so they can learn it

example.en: I teach English at a school.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the right future form: 'Next year I will teach Korean.'
form.why: 가르치- ends in a vowel, so -(으)ㄹ 거예요 adds just ㄹ: 가르칠 거예요.

ko_meaning_en: To use your head to try to understand something

example.en: When I think of my family at night I feel sad.

form.q_en: Pick the ending that means 'when/if'.
form.why: -(으)면 = if/when. 생각하- ends in a vowel, so just add -면: 생각하면.

ko_meaning_en: To do something many times to get good at it

example.en: My younger brother practices taekwondo every day.

form.q_en: I have a test, so I have to practice every day. Pick the 'have to' form.
form.why: -아야/어야 하다 = have to. For 하다 verbs it becomes 해야: 연습해야 해요.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일을 하기 전에 필요한 것을 먼저 하다
ko_meaning_en: To do the needed things before something happens

example.en: Guests were coming in the evening so I prepared food.

form.q_en: Pick the right past form of 준비하다.
form.why: For 하다 verbs, the past polite form is 했어요: 준비했어요.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일이 다 되어서 더 하지 않다
ko_meaning_en: Something is all done and doesn't go on any more

example.en: What time does the class end?

form.q_en: 끝나다 does not take an object. Pick the particle.
form.why: With 끝나다 the class is the subject: 수업 ends in a consonant, so 이. 을 would need the verb 끝내다.

ko_meaning_en: To be on your feet, not sitting or lying

example.en: There were no seats on the bus so I stood the whole way.

form.q_en: Pick the polite request: 'Please stand here.'
form.why: -(으)세요 after a vowel stem: 서 + 세요 → 서세요.

ko_meaning_en: To lay your body down flat on the floor or a bed

example.en: I had a headache so I lay down on the bed.

form.q_en: Pick the right past form of 눕다.
form.why: 눕다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우, so 누 + 웠어요 → 누웠어요.

ko_meaning_en: To move your feet quickly to go forward

example.en: The children are running in the park.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: My leg hurts, so I can't run. Pick the form before 수 없어요.
form.why: -(으)ㄹ 수 없다 = can't. 뛰- ends in a vowel, so add ㄹ: 뛸 수 없어요.

ko_meaning_en: To go from below to above

example.en: I went up a mountain with a friend on the weekend.

form.q_en: Pick the right future form of 올라가다.
form.why: 올라가- ends in a vowel, so -(으)ㄹ 거예요 adds just ㄹ: 올라갈 거예요.

ko_meaning_en: To go from above to below

example.en: I went down to the kitchen to drink some water.

form.q_en: I went down to the first floor and then bought coffee. Pick the 'and then' form.
form.why: 가 + 아서 → 가서, so 내려가서 = 'went down and (then)'.

ko_meaning_en: To have something in your hand or raise it up

example.ko: 가방이 무거워서 혼자 들 수 없어요.
example.roman: Gabangi mugeowoseo honja deul su eopseoyo.
example.en: The bag is heavy so I can't lift it alone.

form.q_en: Pick the right form before 수 있어요: 'Can you hold this bag?'
form.why: 들- already ends in ㄹ, so -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 adds nothing: 들 수 있어요.

ko_meaning_en: To leave a thing in some place

example.en: I put the cup on the desk.

tokens.note: ㅗ in the stem → -았어요; ㅎ is silent

form.q_en: Pick the right polite request: 'Please put your bag here.'
form.why: 놓- ends in a consonant, so it takes -으세요: 놓으세요.

ko_meaning_en: To take hold of something with your hand and not let go

example.en: The child held Mom's hand.

form.q_en: Pick the right past form of 잡다.
form.why: 잡다 is NOT ㅂ-irregular (unlike 덥다); it keeps ㅂ and takes -았어요: 잡았어요.

ko_meaning: 다른 사람의 것을 얼마 동안 쓰려고 받다
ko_meaning_en: To take someone else's thing to use for a while

example.en: I borrowed a little money from a friend.

form.q_en: I borrowed a book and then read it at home. Pick the 'and then' form.
form.why: 빌리 + 어서 → 빌려서. Here -아서/어서 means 'and then (with it)'.

ko_meaning_en: To give back something you borrowed

example.en: I'm going to give the book back to my friend tomorrow.

form.q_en: You have to give back a borrowed book. Pick the 'have to' form.
form.why: 주 + 어야 → 줘야, so 돌려줘야 해요 = 'have to give back'.

ko_meaning_en: A letter sent and received over the internet

example.en: I get a lot of emails every day at work.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the object particle for 이메일.
form.why: 이메일 ends in ㄹ (a consonant), so the object particle is 을, not 를.

ko_meaning_en: A short piece of writing sent by cell phone

example.en: Send me a text when you get home.

form.q_en: Pick the object particle for 문자.
form.why: 문자 ends in a vowel, so the object particle is 를.

ko_meaning: 종이에 써서 다른 사람에게 보내는 글
ko_meaning_en: Writing on paper that you send to someone

example.en: I read the letter my grandmother wrote.

form.q_en: Pick the right modifier: 'the letter (that) Grandma wrote'.
form.why: 쓰- ends in a vowel, so the past noun modifier is -ㄴ: 쓴 편지 = the letter someone wrote.

ko_meaning: 전화나 문자로 다른 사람에게 소식을 알리다
ko_meaning_en: To give someone news by phone or text

example.en: Get in touch if you have time.

form.q_en: Pick the polite 'I will' form with -겠어요.
form.why: -겠어요 attaches to the stem: 연락하 + 겠어요 → 연락하겠어요 ('I will contact you').

ko_meaning_en: To make a phone call and talk

example.en: I called my parents yesterday.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for the person you call.
form.why: Use 에게 for the person you call ('to'). 에서 is for places, and 전화하다 does not take a person as an object with 을.

ko_meaning_en: A phone you carry around and use

example.en: I left my cell phone at home.

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 핸드폰.
form.why: 핸드폰 ends in a consonant (ㄴ), so the subject particle is 이.

ko_meaning: 컴퓨터나 핸드폰으로 여러 가지를 찾고 볼 수 있는 것
ko_meaning_en: What lets you find and see many things on a computer or phone

example.en: I found a cheap plane ticket on the internet.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where you do something online.
form.why: 에서 marks the place where an action happens: 인터넷에서 = on the internet.

ko_meaning_en: Numbers given to something to show which it is

example.en: Write your name and number on your bag.

form.q_en: Pick 'and' after 번호.
form.why: 번호 ends in a vowel, so 'and' is 와. 과 is used after a consonant.

ko_meaning: 사는 곳이나 건물이 있는 곳을 나타낸 것
ko_meaning_en: What shows where someone lives or where a building is

example.en: What is my friend's home address?

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 주소.
form.why: 주소 ends in a vowel, so the subject particle is 가.

ko_meaning: 다른 사람이 모르게 나만 아는 번호
ko_meaning_en: A number only you know, so others can't use it

example.ko: 비밀번호를 몰라서 문을 열 수 없어요.
example.roman: Bimilbeonhoreul mollaseo muneul yeol su eopseoyo.
example.en: I don't know the password so I can't open the door.

form.q_en: Pick the object particle for 비밀번호.
form.ko: 비밀번호___ 몰라서 문을 열 수 없어요.
form.why: 비밀번호 is the object of 모르다 and ends in a vowel, so it takes 를.

ko_meaning_en: Not often, just once in a while

example.en: On weekends I sometimes watch movies alone.

form.q_en: Pick the adverb that fits this positive sentence.
form.why: 가끔 works in a positive sentence. 전혀 and 별로 need a negative, and 아까 (a while ago) needs the past tense.

ko_meaning: 특별한 일이 없을 때 거의 언제나
ko_meaning_en: Almost always, when nothing special is happening

example.en: I usually get up at seven.

form.q_en: I usually don't eat breakfast. Pick the form before 않아요.
form.why: -지 않다 makes a negative: the stem 먹- + 지 않아요.

ko_meaning_en: Not even a little (followed by 안, 못 or 없다)

example.ko: 저는 매운 음식을 전혀 못 먹어요.
example.roman: Jeoneun maeun eumsigeul jeonhyeo mot meogeoyo.
example.en: I can't eat spicy food at all.

form.q_en: 전혀 needs a negative. Pick the right ending.
form.why: 전혀 is used only with negative words like 안, 못 or 없다.

ko_meaning_en: Not that much (followed by 안 or -지 않다)

example.en: It's not that cold today.

form.q_en: This stew is not very spicy. Pick the form before 않아요.
form.why: -지 않다 follows the stem: 맵 + 지 않아요. 별로 goes with negative forms like this.

ko_meaning_en: Not all, but close to all

example.en: I've almost finished my homework.

form.q_en: Pick the word for 'almost': 'Almost all my friends came.'
form.why: 거의 다 = almost all. 전혀 and 별로 need a negative, and 내일 (tomorrow) does not fit the past tense.

ko_meaning_en: Much more than you expected

example.en: These pants are too long.

form.q_en: It was too spicy, so I couldn't eat it. Pick the reason form.
form.why: 맵다 is ㅂ-irregular: 매 + 워서 → 매워서.

ko_meaning_en: Truly, not a lie

example.en: Korean winters are really cold.

form.q_en: This kimchi is really spicy BUT tasty. Pick the 'but' form.
form.why: -지만 attaches straight to the stem: 맵 + 지만 → 맵지만. ㅂ does not change before a consonant.

ko_meaning_en: First among many

example.ko: 저는 과일 중에서 딸기를 제일 좋아해요.
example.roman: Jeoneun gwail jung-eseo ttalgireul jeil joahaeyo.
example.en: Of all fruits I like strawberries the most.

form.q_en: Pick the word: 'Of all seasons I like summer the most.'
form.why: 제일 = the most. 전혀 and 별로 need a negative, and 방금 (just now) does not fit.

ko_meaning_en: More than something else

example.en: I want to eat more rice.

form.q_en: Pick the particle for 'than': 'The train is faster than the bus.'
form.why: N보다 더 = more than N, so 버스보다 더 빨라요 = faster than the bus.

ko_meaning_en: Without forgetting, whatever happens

example.en: Tomorrow I'll be sure to come early.

form.q_en: You must do your homework. Pick the 'have to' form.
form.why: 하다 + -아야/어야 → 해야, so 꼭 해야 해요 = must do.

ko_meaning_en: Just yourself, without anyone else

example.en: My older brother lives alone in Seoul.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: I plan to live alone next year. Pick the 'plan to' form.
form.why: 살- ends in ㄹ, so -(으)려고 adds just 려고: 살려고 해요 = plan to live.

ko_meaning_en: All, with nothing left out

example.en: Everyone in my family is tall.

form.q_en: Pick the right present form of 크다.
form.why: In 크다, ㅡ drops before -어요: 크 + 어요 → 커요.

ko_meaning_en: Everything, with nothing left

example.en: I was hungry so I ate all the rice.

form.q_en: Pick the reason form of 고프다.
form.why: In 고프다, ㅡ drops, and the vowel before it (ㅗ) brings -아서: 고파서.

ko_meaning_en: Very nicely; without mistakes

example.en: My older sister sings really well.

form.q_en: Pick the word that means 'well' (not the adjective 좋다).
form.why: 잘 is the adverb 'well' and can go before a verb. 좋은, 좋아요 and 좋다 are forms of the adjective 좋다.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일을 할 수 없다는 뜻의 말
ko_meaning_en: A word meaning you are unable to do something

example.en: I hurt my leg so I can't play soccer.

tokens.note: 못 goes right before the verb

form.q_en: 못 가요 means the same as ___ 수 없어요. Pick the form.
form.why: 못 가요 = 갈 수 없어요 (cannot go). -(으)ㄹ 수 없다 needs the -(으)ㄹ form: 갈.

ko_meaning: 앞의 말과 뒤의 말을 이어 주는 말
ko_meaning_en: A word that joins what comes before and after

example.en: And I bought eggs too.

form.q_en: Pick the word for 'and' that adds another fact.
form.why: 그리고 adds another fact. 하지만 shows contrast, 그러면 a condition and 그래서 a result, which don't fit.

ko_meaning: 이야기를 바꾸거나 앞과 다른 말을 할 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: Used to change the topic or say something different

example.en: By the way, what's your name?

form.q_en: Pick the word that changes the topic ('by the way').
form.why: 그런데 turns to a new topic. 그래서/그러니까 give a result and 그래도 means 'even so', which don't fit.

ko_meaning: 앞의 일 때문에 뒤의 일이 생길 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: Used when the earlier thing causes the later thing

example.en: So I couldn't go to school today.

form.q_en: Pick the word that shows a result.
form.why: 그래서 = so (result). 그래도 and 하지만 show contrast, and 그런데 changes the topic.

ko_meaning: 앞의 말과 반대되는 말을 할 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: Used to say the opposite of what came before

example.en: But the price is too high.

form.q_en: Pick the word that shows contrast.
form.why: 하지만 = but/however. 그래서 and 그러니까 give a result, and 그러면 a condition.

ko_meaning: 앞의 말이 맞으면 또는 그렇게 하면
ko_meaning_en: If what was said is so, or if you do that

example.en: Then please come again tomorrow.

form.q_en: Pick the word meaning 'in that case'.
form.why: 그러면 = then, in that case. 그래도 and 하지만 show contrast, and 그리고 just adds.

ko_meaning: 앞의 일이 있어도 뒤의 일이 바뀌지 않을 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: Used when the later thing stays the same despite the earlier thing

example.en: Even so I exercise every day.

form.q_en: Pick the word meaning 'even so'.
form.ko: 비가 많이 와요. ___ 산에 갈 거예요.
form.why: 그래도 = even so. 그래서, 그러니까 and 그러면 would make going up the mountain a result of the rain.

ko_meaning: 앞의 말이 뒤의 말의 이유일 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: Used when the earlier words are the reason for the later ones

example.en: So be sure to take an umbrella.

form.q_en: Before a request, which 'so' is natural?
form.why: 그래서 cannot come before a request or suggestion; use 그러니까. 하지만 and 그래도 show contrast.

ko_meaning: 한 번 더; 그 위에 더
ko_meaning_en: One more time; on top of that

example.ko: 어제 간 식당에 또 가고 싶어요.
example.roman: Eoje gan sikdang-e tto gago sipeoyo.
example.en: I want to go again to the restaurant I went to yesterday.

form.q_en: Pick the past noun modifier: 'the restaurant I went to yesterday'.
form.why: A past action before a noun takes -(으)ㄴ: 어제 간 식당. -는 is present and -(으)ㄹ is future.

ko_meaning: 꼭은 아니지만 그럴 것 같을 때 쓰는 말
ko_meaning_en: Used when something is likely but not certain

example.en: It will probably rain tomorrow.

form.q_en: 아마 goes with a guess about the future. Pick the ending.
form.why: 아마 usually comes with -(으)ㄹ 거예요 to make a guess: 올 거예요.

ko_meaning_en: Very fast, in a way you didn't expect

example.ko: 갑자기 비가 와서 옷이 다 젖었어요.
example.roman: Gapjagi biga waseo osi da jeojeosseoyo.
example.en: It suddenly rained so my clothes got all wet.

form.q_en: It suddenly rained, so I bought an umbrella. Pick the reason form.
form.why: 오 + 아서 → 와서. Don't put the past tense before -아서/어서.

ko_meaning_en: A very short time ago

example.en: My friend just got home.

form.q_en: 방금 talks about the past. Pick the ending.
form.why: 방금 means 'just now', so the verb must be past: 출발했어요.

ko_meaning_en: A little while ago

example.en: The rice cake I ate earlier was really delicious.

form.q_en: Pick the past noun modifier: 'the rice cake I ate earlier'.
form.why: A past action before a noun takes -(으)ㄴ. 먹- ends in a consonant, so 먹은.

ko_meaning_en: After a little time passes

example.en: Let's have lunch together in a bit.

form.q_en: 이따가 is about later. Pick the ending.
form.why: 이따가 points to the near future, so use -(으)ㄹ 거예요: 전화할 거예요.

ko_meaning_en: Without stopping

example.en: The baby keeps crying at night.

form.q_en: The baby kept crying, so I couldn't sleep. Pick the reason form.
form.why: 울다 has ㅜ, so it takes -어서: 울어서. Don't add the past tense before -어서.

ko_meaning_en: In a very short time

example.en: If you take this medicine you'll get better soon.

form.q_en: Pick the right polite form of 낫다.
form.why: 낫다 is ㅅ-irregular: ㅅ drops before a vowel, so 나 + 아요 → 나아요 (no contraction).

ko_meaning_en: A room at school where classes are held

example.en: There are ten students in the classroom.

form.q_en: We study IN the classroom (an action). Pick the particle.
form.why: Use 에서 for the place where an action happens. 에 is for where something is or where you go.

ko_meaning: 글씨를 쓰려고 종이를 묶어 만든 책
ko_meaning_en: A book of paper bound together for writing

example.en: I wrote down what the teacher said in my notebook.

tokens.note: 에 marks where it is written

form.q_en: Pick the particle for where the words end up.
form.why: 에 marks the spot where something is written or put: 공책에 쓰다.

ko_meaning_en: A writing tool made of wood

example.en: Bring a pencil to the exam.

form.q_en: Pick the object particle for 연필.
form.why: 연필 ends in ㄹ (a consonant), so the object particle is 을.

ko_meaning_en: A thing for rubbing out pencil writing

example.en: Can I borrow an eraser?

form.q_en: Pick the form before 수 있어요: 'Can I borrow ...?'
form.why: 빌리- ends in a vowel, so -(으)ㄹ 수 있다 adds just ㄹ: 빌릴 수 있어요.

ko_meaning: 말의 뜻을 찾을 수 있는 책
ko_meaning_en: A book where you can look up what words mean

example.en: Look up words you don't know in the dictionary.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the noun modifier: 'words you don't know'.
form.why: Verbs take -는 before a noun in the present: 모르는 말.

ko_meaning_en: Work you do to earn money

example.en: My dad is a doctor by profession.

form.q_en: Pick the right ending: 'My sister's job is a teacher.'
form.why: 선생님 ends in a consonant, so it takes 이에요. 예요 follows a vowel.

ko_meaning: 여러 사람이 모여서 어떤 일을 이야기하는 것
ko_meaning_en: People coming together to talk about something

example.en: I'm busy because I have a meeting in the afternoon.

tokens.note: 가 marks the subject after a vowel

form.q_en: Pick the reason form of 있다.
form.why: 있다 has ㅣ in the stem, so it takes -어서: 있어서.

ko_meaning_en: To go to the office to work

example.en: I take the subway to work every day.

form.q_en: I plan to go to work early tomorrow. Pick the 'plan to' form.
form.why: -(으)려고 하다 = plan to. 출근하- ends in a vowel, so add -려고: 출근하려고 해요.

ko_meaning_en: To finish work and leave the office

example.en: I'm going to meet a friend after work.

form.q_en: Call me when you leave work. Pick the 'when/if' form.
form.why: -(으)면 = if/when. 퇴근하- ends in a vowel, so add -면: 퇴근하면.

ko_meaning_en: Before the usual time

example.en: I'm tired today so I'll go to bed early.

form.q_en: Pick the adverb meaning 'early'.
form.why: 일찍 is the adverb that goes before a verb. 이른, 일러요 and 이르다 are forms of the adjective 이르다.

ko_meaning: 다른 사람과 언제 무엇을 할지 정한 것
ko_meaning_en: What you decided with someone about when and what to do

example.en: I have plans with a friend this evening.

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 약속.
form.why: 약속 ends in a consonant, so the subject particle is 이.

ko_meaning: 여러 사람이 모여서 먹고 마시고 노는 것
ko_meaning_en: People getting together to eat, drink and have fun

example.en: I'm going to have a birthday party on Saturday.

form.q_en: Pick the object particle for 파티.
form.why: 파티 ends in a vowel, so the object particle is 를.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일로 여러 사람이 모이는 것
ko_meaning_en: People coming together for some purpose

example.en: Who is coming to this gathering?

form.q_en: Pick the right subject form of 'who'.
form.why: 누구 + 가 becomes 누가. 누구가 is not used.

ko_meaning_en: To ask someone to come to a gathering or party

example.en: I invited my friends to my house.

form.q_en: Pick the right future form of 초대하다.
form.why: 초대하- ends in a vowel, so add -ㄹ 거예요. The ending is spelled 거예요, not 거에요.

ko_meaning_en: To come or do something after the set time

example.en: I missed the bus so I was late for work.

form.q_en: If you are late, contact me. Pick the 'if' form.
form.why: 늦- ends in a consonant, so -(으)면 becomes -으면: 늦으면.

ko_meaning: 개, 고양이, 소처럼 움직이며 사는 것
ko_meaning_en: Living things that move, like dogs, cats and cows

example.en: Lots of animals live at Grandma's house.

form.q_en: Pick the subject particle for 동물.
form.why: 동물 ends in a consonant (ㄹ), so the subject particle is 이.

ko_meaning_en: A small, young dog

example.en: I took a walk in the park with my puppy.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick 'with' after 강아지 (ends in a vowel).
form.why: 강아지 ends in a vowel, so 'with' is 와 (or 하고), not 과.

ko_meaning_en: A big animal with lots of fur

example.en: It would be scary to see a bear in the mountains.

tokens.note: 에서 marks where an action happens

form.q_en: Pick the right future (guess) form of 무섭다.
form.why: 무섭다 is ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ becomes 우, so 무서 + 울 거예요 → 무서울 거예요.

ko_meaning: 귀가 길고 빨리 뛰는 작은 동물
ko_meaning_en: A small animal with long ears that hops fast

example.en: Rabbits have long ears.

form.q_en: Pick the topic particle for 토끼.
form.why: 토끼 ends in a vowel, so the topic particle is 는. 은 follows a consonant.

ko_meaning: 몸에 검은 줄이 있는 크고 무서운 동물
ko_meaning_en: A big, scary animal with black stripes

example.en: I saw a tiger for the first time yesterday.

form.q_en: Pick the right past form of 보다.
form.why: 보다 has ㅗ, so it takes -았어요, and 보 + 았 contracts to 봤: 봤어요.

ko_meaning: 전에 있었던 일을 잊지 않고 생각하다
ko_meaning_en: To keep something from before in mind and not forget it

example.en: Do you remember my name?

form.q_en: I can't remember that person's name. Pick the form before 수 없어요.
form.why: 기억하- ends in a vowel, so -(으)ㄹ 수 없다 adds just ㄹ: 기억할 수 없어요.

ko_meaning_en: To be unable to recall something you knew

example.en: I'm really sorry I forgot your birthday.

tokens.note: -어서 gives the reason for the apology

form.q_en: Pick the right past form of 잊다.
form.why: 잊다 has ㅣ in the stem, so it takes -었어요: 잊었어요.

ko_meaning: 어떤 일이 그렇게 되면 좋겠다고 생각하다
ko_meaning_en: To think it would be good if something happened

example.en: I wish for my family's happiness.

form.q_en: Pick the correct spelling (not the spoken form).
form.why: 바라다 + 아요 → 바라요. 바래요 is common in speech but is a spelling mistake.

ko_meaning_en: To want to have or do something

example.en: Choose the color you want.

form.q_en: Pick the present noun modifier of 원하다.
form.why: Verbs take -는 before a noun in the present: 원하는 색깔.

ko_meaning: 다른 사람이 알 수 있게 말해 주다
ko_meaning_en: To tell someone so that they know

example.en: I told the students the exam date.

form.q_en: Everyone must be told the meeting time. Pick the 'have to' form.
form.why: 알리 + 어야 → 알려야, so 알려야 해요 = have to let (them) know.
